To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) joint power control and beamforming is a promising means to maximize throughput for CDMA wireless uplinks with multiple base station antennas; (2) the optimization problem that arises in this context can be solved using iterative algorithms that alternate between power control steps and beamforming steps; (3) the resulting algorithms converge to a locally optimal solution, and (4) simulations show that this locally optimal solution can yield a significant improvement in throughput.

the proposed joint beamforming and adaptive power control algorithms converge to locally optimal power vectors and beamforming arrays, and that the resulting uplink throughput is significantly better than the performance of conventional power control algorithms.
